blocks.text: A cache keeps a response so it may be reused. Cache headers tell the browser how long a response can stay fresh.

Use a local test page and browser developer tools. Code samples show a page choice or a measurement. Compare before and after under the same conditions; exact timings depend on the device and network.

blocks.code:
For a versioned asset such as app.a1b2c3.js, a static host may send:
Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable

For HTML that changes, use a policy that lets the browser check for updates.
blocks.title: Understand browser caching

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `Cache-Control` is a response header sent by the host. It tells a browser how a response may be reused.

blocks.text: A file whose address changes with its contents can be cached for a long time. HTML needs a policy that still delivers updates.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Do not give changing files the same long-lived immutable address. These are host response headers, not HTML tags.
